title: Delete key doesn't delete a selected vector shape (subselection vs standard-selection mismatch)
description:
USER-REPORTED: pressing Delete (or Backspace) on the keyboard with a vector shape selected does NOT delete it. The shape stays on the stage / in the document.

== REPRO (e2e, :1420) ==
Draw a vector rect with the Rect tool, switch to the Selection tool, single-click the shape, press Delete then Backspace.
  - shapes after draw = 1
  - selectedShapeIds after selecting the vector shape = []  (EMPTY)
  - shapes after Delete = 1  (NOT removed)
  - shapes after Backspace = 1  (NOT removed)
Same for brush/oval-drawn fills (all commit the same vector 'shape' display object and take the identical Selection-tool path).

== SCOPE ==
Delete WORKS for the standard/live selection types and FAILS only for vector shapes:
  - TEXT object: select with Selection tool -> selectedShapeIds = ['text-1-...'] (POPULATED); Delete -> text objects 1->0 (REMOVED). WORKS.
  - SYMBOL/MovieClip instance: code path is identical to text (standard onShapeSelect -> selectedShapeIds), so Delete works for it too.
  - VECTOR SHAPE (rect/oval/brush fill): selectedShapeIds stays [] (goes into the SUBSELECTION model instead); Delete no-ops. BROKEN.

== ROOT CAUSE (file:line) ==
A selection-model mismatch introduced by the planar-merge cutover (the 1331 family). The Selection tool now ALWAYS uses the subselection (partial face/segment) path for vector shapes, but the Delete command only consults the STANDARD selection.

1. packages/authoring-ui/src/Shell.tsx:1116
     const partialSelectEnabled = toolState.activeTool === 'selection';
   -> the Selection tool is ALWAYS in partial-select mode for vector shapes.

2. packages/authoring-ui/src/StageArea.tsx:2620-2641 (pointerdown shape-hit branch)
     if (partialSelectEnabled && onSubSelect && !e.shiftKey) {
       ... onSubSelect(sel); ... return;   // SUBSELECTION ONLY
     }
   Clicking a hit vector shape calls onSubSelect(...) (-> setSubSelection in Shell), and RETURNS BEFORE ever calling onShapeSelect. So selectedShapeIds is never populated for a vector shape.
   Contrast: the symbol-instance branch (StageArea.tsx:2671-2687) and the text branch (StageArea.tsx:2698+) BOTH call onShapeSelect(hit.id, shift) -> setSelectedShapeIds, the standard selection path. That is why Delete works for symbols/text but not vector shapes.

3. packages/authoring-ui/src/commands/editor.ts:11-12, :27
     const hasSelection = (ctx) => ctx.ui.getState().selectedShapeIds.length > 0;
     { id: 'edit.delete', ... isEnabled: hasSelection, run: run((e) => e.deleteSelected()) }
   With selectedShapeIds empty, edit.delete is DISABLED and no-ops. The keyboard handler (dispatch/keyboard.ts:44) correctly maps Delete/Backspace -> 'edit.delete', and preventDefaults it, but the command's isEnabled gate (and deleteSelected itself) sees an empty standard selection.

4. packages/authoring-ui/src/Shell.tsx:1691-1703 (handleDeleteSelected)
     if (selectedShapeIds.length === 0) return;   // early return
     ... iterates selectedShapeIds, removeDisplayObject(...) ...
   deleteSelected operates ENTIRELY on selectedShapeIds and never consults subSelection, so even if the command ran it would delete nothing for a vector shape.

== 1331 / PLANAR-CUTOVER FAMILY ==
Yes. Same root cause family as task 1331 (no live drag preview for vector shapes): the planar-merge P5 cutover made the Selection tool route vector-shape selection through the SUBSELECTION model (partialSelectEnabled-always-on, subselection.ts face/segment keys) instead of the standard display-object selection. Any selection-dependent behavior that reads selectedShapeIds (Delete, and likely cut/copy/duplicate/nudge/group/arrange, which are all gated on selectedShapeIds) is broken for vector shapes selected via the Selection tool. Symbols and text still use the standard/live selection path, so they are unaffected.

== FIX DIRECTION ==
Make Delete consult the subselection for vector shapes. Two viable approaches:
  (A) When a vector shape is selected via the subselection path, ALSO populate selectedShapeIds with the shape id (so Delete/cut/copy/duplicate/nudge/etc. all work uniformly). i.e. in StageArea.tsx:2620 branch, call onShapeSelect(hit.id) (or set the standard selection alongside the SubSelection) in addition to onSubSelect. Cleanest, fixes the whole family of selection-ops at once. Verify it doesn't break the split-on-move drag / face-level partial editing.
  (B) Make handleDeleteSelected (Shell.tsx:1691) and edit.delete's isEnabled (editor.ts:11) ALSO consult subSelection: when subSelection is set, delete the selected vector shape (whole shape) or the selected region/face. This keeps the two selection models separate but requires touching every selection-op command.
Acceptance must be the Ruffle/stage e2e (per the Verification learning -- byte/unit tests are not sufficient): draw a vector rect, select with the Selection tool, press Delete, assert the shape is gone from the doc AND the stage; confirm Backspace too; confirm symbol/text deletion still works (regression).
